newsitem.title: UK: West Africa, UKC tankers firm on strong demand.
newsitem.headline: West Africa, UKC tankers firm on strong demand.

text.p: West Africa/U.S. 130,000 tonne dirty tanker rates firmed on Wednesday on heavy enquiry, but some brokers said there was little scope for a further rise.
One broker said that after rates had risen from W102.5 to W105/107.5, the market was now "steady rather than strong."

"I don't see it going up much further. There is a natural cap when VLCCs double up stems," he added. referring to the practice of combining 130,000 tonne cargoes onto very large crude carriers when there is sufficient demand.
Another broker was slightly more bullish, saying, "(West Africa) rates may move up slightly.
"At least I don't think they will go down this week or early next."

The inter/U.K.-Cont market firmed sharply on fog-related delays and a lack of tonnage. Rates varied considerably according to dates and vessel quality, but brokers put the market for 80,000 tonners at about W140, against W130 on Tuesday.

Middle East VLCC rates edged up on a lack of vessels and as early April cargoes began to be fixed. Brokers said most destinations were up 2.5 points, with Mideast/west voyages at W57.5, Japan at W65 and the Red Sea and Singapore at W60.
The cross-Mediterranean sector also edged up in step with West Africa, with 80,000 tonne cargoes fixed at W107.5-110 and 130,000 tonnes at W100-105.

"A lot of private requirements are keeping the market busy. Officially there are not too many requirements but...the market is surviving on private cargoes," said one broker. About 80 percent of Med fixtures were currently private and confidential, he added.
Fuel oil was steady, with inter-U.K./Cont 25,000 cargoes at W190 and cross-Med at W220. "Inter-UKC may start to look firmer as there's quite a bit of enquiry around," one broker said.
